claims.supported_claim: SeaORM SQLite acquires per query by default, and query_all uses fetch_all; SqliteRow/QueryResult and result conversions are public. NW must perform its own bounded collect and retain a pinned Session lease.
claims.limitations: Only the listed actual reading ranges are covered; upstream or NativeWeave Rust, C# and AOT were not compiled/run, and design inferences are not upgraded to implementation validation.

claims.supported_claim: Each connection starts its own OS thread with bounded command channel. Execute has bounded row channel. Row send failure stops iteration; this does not preempt sqlite3_step already executing.
claims.limitations: ['A bounded row/item channel does not prove retained bytes bounded; NativeWeave must bound connection threads, accepted work, row bytes, and waiting payloads.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: Begin success with lost acknowledgement triggers immediate rollback; rollback failure exits the worker. Successful Commit/Rollback with lost ack sets ignore_next_start_rollback to avoid rolling back a completed transaction when the Transaction later drops.
claims.limitations: ['Worker acknowledgement is not the C# application result, and lost acknowledgement must not be translated into a false rollback conclusion. Custom BEGIN validation moved into worker in 0.9.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: start_rollback and shutdown synchronously send into the bounded command channel. Shutdown handling drops connection references before ack and then exits its loop.
claims.limitations: ['These send calls can block. They must not run directly in NativeWeave nonblocking request_stop/try_retire/ReleaseHandle/reverse callback. Ack occurs before closure return; it is not an OS JoinHandle proof.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: Graceful close may execute PRAGMA optimize, then requests worker shutdown, drops self and awaits confirmation. close_hard drops self and immediately returns; flush is no-op.
claims.limitations: ['close_hard/Drop/flush are not proof of worker completion or NativeWeave quiescence. Run potentially blocking cleanup from a controlled native blocking lane/supervisor, keep ownership until confirmed.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: Progress handler uses owned boxed closure, only one handler per connection; false interrupts, replacement removes/frees old handler. C shim catch_unwind maps ordinary panic to interrupt. ConnectionState clears statements before hook removal and handle drop.
claims.limitations: ['Handler must not modify the connection; avoid arbitrary managed user callbacks or allocations per VM poll. Its catch/unwrap_or_default does not imply universal panic-payload destructor safety.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: Statement reset/clear_bindings precede bind. step yields row/result/error; dropping iterator calls statement.reset().ok().
claims.limitations: ["Drop swallows reset failure; NativeWeave needs an explicit reuse proof or conservative discard, not 'Drop means clean'. StatementHandle::reset internals not read in this task."] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: begin/commit/rollback delegate to worker; start_rollback only enqueues and ignores the enqueue error at manager boundary; depth is separately observed.
claims.limitations: ['No executed transaction/cancellation test in this research.'] Reader is interop_design; not independently reread by database_design.

claims.supported_claim: Tests assert progress-triggered interrupted database error and correct closure-state identity; repeated handler replacement preserves expected Arc strong count and removal frees the captured owner.
